question: What does it take to become a Tier 1 organization on Stellar — how many validators, what uptime, and how do you actually get in?

golden.answer: A Tier 1 organization runs three geographically dispersed Full Validators, each publishing its own history archive, with sustained 99.9%+ uptime and SEP-1 and SEP-20 self-verification. It is not granted by SDF or bought by staking: other Tier 1 organizations must choose to include you in their quorum sets, which takes months. Three validators let 2-of-3 still vote for you during a failure.
keyFacts: Requires three geographically dispersed Full Validators, each with its own archive.
Tier 1 status comes from other Tier 1 orgs including you in their quorum sets.
It is not granted by SDF application or staking XLM.
avoid: Do NOT claim a stake, fee, SDF approval, or a validator count other than three.

sources.note: class inferred at migration; re-checked live 2026-11-02 (golden audit, batch protocol-core-05)

corroboration.claim: Tier 1 status is earned by other Tier 1 orgs including you in their quorum sets (trust / invitation) — not granted by application to SDF, and not by staking XLM or paying a fee.

evidence.note: Exact quotes: ‘no central authority dictates whose vote is required for consensus.’ ‘There are no monetary rewards for being a validator on the Stellar network.’
Exact quotes: ‘Joining is not a unilateral SDF decision’; ‘every existing Tier 1 organization independently decides whether to add you to their quorum set.’

Dated web sweep query `Stellar Tier 1 organization quorum set invitation SDF staking fee`: Range says each validator chooses trusted peers, `Tier 1 is not a designation an organization can claim on its own`, operators coordinate with existing operators, and they run `not for financial return`. No primary result described an SDF application, stake, or fee.

corroboration.claim: Three geographically dispersed Full Validators, 99.9%+ uptime, SEP-1 and SEP-20, months not weeks, inclusion by other orgs

evidence.note: Run three geographically dispersed Full Validators, achieve sustained 99.9%+ uptime … complete SEP-20 and SEP-1 self-verification … Expect a process measured in months, not weeks.

evidence: Live A 2026-11-14: https://developers.stellar.org/docs/validators/tier-1-orgs -- 'Run three geographically dispersed Full Validators, achieve sustained 99.9%+ uptime … complete SEP-20 and SEP-1 self-verification … Expect a process measured in months, not weeks.'

truth.notes:
Three full validators + quorum-set trust are defining. Trap is staking/application framing or wrong count.
Also good if the answer: Mentions the ~99.9%+ uptime target with 24/7 monitoring. | Mentions SEP-1 (stellar.toml) and SEP-20 self-verification as requirements. | Explains the 'why three': 2-of-3 of your nodes can still vote on your behalf during maintenance/failure.
Golden cites: The Tier 1 Organizations page on developers.stellar.org/docs/validators/tier-1-orgs.
